sections.html:
Abington Township requires an affidavit at or before settlement on any single-family, two-family or multifamily dwelling. The seller swears that the house shows a clear street address, has smoke detectors and has at least one carbon monoxide detector. Under Resolution 92-008, a deed is not accepted for registration unless this certification comes with it.

Ordinance 1894 spells out the rules, and a buyer's agent will check them.

Abington Township detector and address rules
RequirementStandard
Address numeralsAt least three inches high on the street side of the structure, visible from the center of the street
Smoke detectorsOne on each level and in each bedroom or sleeping area
Carbon monoxide detectorNo more than 40 feet from every sleeping area
EquipmentUL rated and approved detectors

Breaking the ordinance is a summary offense that can bring a fine of $1,000 at most, up to 30 days in jail, or both, and every day of a continuing violation is charged separately. The affidavit form is available from the township. Smoke and CO alarms cost little, and installing them before listing removes a closing delay.

sections.h2: No use and occupancy permit for homes
sections.html:
Abington does not have a use and occupancy permit for residential properties. Use and occupancy review applies to commercial properties, new businesses and business transfers, and includes a Fire Marshal inspection.

A typical Abington house sale is therefore lighter on municipal paperwork than in towns that demand a resale inspection. The detector affidavit is the main township requirement. Any building work you did without a permit is a separate question. Ask the Code Enforcement Division before listing if you finished a basement, built a deck or added a bathroom.

A homeowner's real estate tax bill is split among the township, the Abington School District, a school referendum levy and Montgomery County, which includes the community college. The school district portion is 39.8992 mills, the largest piece by far.

The township levies a realty transfer tax of 1 percent, collected by Montgomery County, on top of the state's 1 percent. Ask your closing agent whether the school district adds a share on your deed. Some transfers are exempt, such as property passing by will or intestate succession.

Abington does not assess property. The Montgomery County Board of Assessments does, and the last countywide reassessment was in 1998. The township bill, which also covers sewer and refuse, is mailed in the first week of February for a January to December year. The school bill follows in the first week of July and runs July to June.

Abington is a first-class township in Montgomery County and a first-ring suburb of Philadelphia, with neighborhoods including Willow Grove, Roslyn, Glenside, Rydal and Meadowbrook. The mid 2025 population is 58,656. Owners live in 77.3 percent of occupied homes, a typical owned home is valued at $391,800, median rent is $1,493 and median household income is $103,645. The Abington School District is separate from township government.

Sellers here generally choose among three routes. An agent listing reaches the widest pool of buyers, and it also means staging, showings and waiting on a buyer's financing and inspection. Selling without an agent saves the commission but leaves the paperwork, from the detector affidavit to the deed, in your hands.

A direct cash sale skips showings and repairs. It suits an inherited house, a tenant-occupied property, a house with code or maintenance issues, or a seller who needs a firm closing date. A cash buyer's price reflects the work the house needs, so weigh it against what a repaired and listed house would net once fees, repairs and months of carrying costs come out.

Whichever route you pick, the same Abington steps apply: the detector certification, the tax figures above and a recorded deed at the Montgomery County Recorder of Deeds.

sections.h2: How do I handle an inherited or tenant-occupied house?
sections.html:
With an inherited house, settle first who can sign for the estate, because title must be in order before a deed can be recorded. Title passing through an estate carries no state transfer tax, though the later sale does.

With a tenant in place, read the lease before you list. Showings and possession dates depend on its terms and on Pennsylvania landlord and tenant law. Buyers who plan to keep the tenant will ask for the lease and rent history, and the detector rules cover rentals sold in the township too.

For questions about the township tax sheet, call the Abington tax office at 267-536-1024 on weekdays between 8 am and 4 pm. Owners of a primary residence can apply for a homestead exclusion through the Montgomery County Board of Assessments, and applications must arrive by March 1 to reduce the school tax bill.

Approved owners are not asked to refile annually, but a move or a change of title means applying again. A buyer who will live in the house should plan to apply after closing.

sections.h2: Getting an Abington house ready to close
sections.html:
A few steps in order keep a township sale on schedule.

  1. Walk the house with the detector rules in hand: numerals at least three inches high, a smoke detector on each level and in each sleeping area, and a carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping area.
  2. Replace or add detectors as needed, and make sure they are UL rated.
  3. Get the affidavit form from the township and sign it at or before settlement. The deed is not accepted for registration without it.
  4. Ask the closing agent about the 1 percent township transfer tax and the state's 1 percent, and who pays what under the contract.
  5. If unpermitted work was done, call the Code Enforcement Division before listing.

Sellers taking a cash offer still sign the same affidavit, but they skip showings, repair negotiations and the wait for a buyer's mortgage approval.

faqs.q: Does Abington require a smoke and carbon monoxide certification when I sell?
faqs.a: Yes. Ordinance 1894 requires smoke detectors on each level and in each bedroom, plus a carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping area, with a seller's affidavit at or before settlement.

faqs.q: Is there a residential use and occupancy permit in Abington?
faqs.a: No. The township has no use and occupancy permit for residential properties. That review applies to commercial buildings and business transfers.
The township levies a 1 percent real estate transfer tax, collected by Montgomery County. The state adds its own 1 percent. Ask the closing agent whether any other local share applies.

faqs.q: Who assesses property in Abington Township?
faqs.a: The Montgomery County Board of Assessments, not the township. The last countywide reassessment was in 1998, and interim bills reflect changes such as additions or demolitions.

faqs.q: When must I apply for the homestead exclusion?
faqs.a: Applications must be in the Board of Assessments' hands by March 1 to cut the school tax bill. Approved owners are not asked to refile annually, but a move or a change of title means applying again.
